newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan panel calls for sweeping telecom decontrol.
newsitem.headline: Japan panel calls for sweeping telecom decontrol.

text.p: A subcommittee of an advisory panel to the prime minister called on Thursday for sweeping deregulation of Japan's telecommunications market, the head of the subcommittee told reporters.
The subcommittee presented deregulation proposals to the advisory council, which is expected to finalise its recommendations in December.
The proposals, including the dismantling of regulations which hinder firms from entering Japan's telecommunications market, were mostly the same as measures considered by the government.
Government officials have said new measures would be aimed at accelerating the implementation of a package deregulation of steps which the government announced in March this year.
The subcommittee called for the scrapping of regulations which distinguish between domestic telecommunications operators and those specialising in international services.

It also proposed that an independent body be set up to mediate and monitor moves by other communications operators to connect to local telephone lines dominated by Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) in order to stimulate competition.
